mainTopic: Walls that fall or are missing: a slanted roof, a קרפף breached into a חצר, and enclosing large orchards
overview: This amud opens mid-discussion. If the covered part of the קרפף had a flat roof like an אכסדרה, everyone would agree that פי תקרה יורד וסותם, so the case must be a slanted roof shaped like a hammock. Next, רבי זירא says a קרפף fully breached into a חצר is forbidden, because the added space pushes it over בית סאתיים. רב יוסף objects that the חצר was already open for carrying. אביי answers that even according to רבי שמעון, the space where the walls stood is new space. רב חסדא's ruling, that the חצר stays permitted and only the קרפף is forbidden, is explained the same way: only a קרפף has a size limit. Then come two real-life cases. When a mansion's outer wall fell, רב פפי ruled that its inner walls cannot enclose the orchard, because they were built for the inside. Finally, רב הונא בר חיננא builds reed fences so the ריש גלותא can eat in his orchard pavilion on שבת, and the amud ends as רבא goes to react, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A flat roof would count as closed; the case is a slanted roof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that רבא and רבי זירא argue about whether a roof's edge counts as a wall. If the roof were flat like an אכסדרה, everyone would agree it does. The case under discussion is a slanted, hammock-like roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were built like an enclosed porch, then indeed everyone would agree. What case are we dealing with here? One where it was built like a hammock.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on an earlier suggestion about the case. It says that with a flat roof there would be no argument, so the case must involve a slanted roof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A flat roof lets us apply פי תקרה יורד וסותם: we imagine the roof's edge coming down to the ground and closing the area. That idea does not work for a slanted roof shaped like a hammock. So the disagreement can only be about a slanted roof, where this idea does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: A covered porch or veranda with a flat roof
Yes, indeed; that is correct
What case are we dealing with here?
A hammock; here, a slanted or sagging roof
The edge of a roof is treated as coming down and closing off the area

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase הכי נמי does not mean the earlier suggestion was right. It means: in a flat-roof case everyone would agree, so the argument cannot be about that case.

phrases.english: If it were made like an enclosed veranda (with a flat roof)
phrases.notes: A flat roof, where the edge can be seen as coming down to form a wall

phrases.english: indeed, so it would be (everyone would agree).
With what are we dealing here?
phrases.notes: This is how the גמרא signals it's going to explain a narrower, specific case.

phrases.english: Where he made it like a hammock (slanted).
phrases.notes: A slanted roof cannot be seen as coming down to close the area

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דַּעֲבִידָא כִּי אַכְסַדְרָה הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects a suggestion on the previous amud about the basis of the רבא and רבי זירא dispute
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the dispute as being about פי תקרה יורד וסותם in a flat-roof case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: With a flat roof everyone would agree, so the dispute must be about a slanted, hammock-like roof

steps.title: רבי זירא agrees a fully breached קרפף is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says he agrees that a קרפף fully breached into a חצר is forbidden for carrying. The reason is that the חצר's space joins the קרפף and makes it larger than בית סאתיים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: I agree that a קרפף that was breached along its full width into a courtyard is forbidden. What is the reason? Because the courtyard's space makes it too big.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא names a case where even he agrees carrying in the קרפף is forbidden. The גמרא asks for his reason, and the answer is that the חצר's space adds to the קרפף's size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרפף not fenced in for living purposes may be used for carrying only up to בית סאתיים. When the entire wall between it and a חצר falls, the two areas become one open space. That extra space pushes the קרפף over the limit, so carrying in it becomes forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: An enclosed area, like a storage yard, not fenced in for living purposes
Breached along its full width (the whole wall is gone)
I agree
Makes it excessive, pushing it over the size limit
An area big enough to plant two סאה of seed; the limit for carrying in a קרפף

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that space added from outside can turn a permitted קרפף into a forbidden one. It sets up the debate that follows.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
And I agree regarding a karpef
that was breached along its full width into a courtyard
that it is forbidden (to carry in it).
What is the reason?
Because the courtyard's space makes it excessive (over two beit se'a).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case where רבי זירא agrees with the stricter ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קרפף fully breached into a חצר is forbidden, because the חצר's space joins it and puts it over בית סאתיים

steps.title: רב יוסף objects: how can permitted space make it forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges רבי זירא's reason. One could already carry between the חצר and the קרפף. So how can the חצר's space now make the קרפף forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: Can space that was permitted to it make it forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks the reason רבי זירא just gave. He asks how space that was already open for carrying could cause a ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף assumes one could already carry from the חצר to the קרפף. If so, the חצר's space was never a problem for the קרפף. It seems unfair that the same space now forbids the קרפף just because the wall fell.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objected to it
Space, air, or area
That is permitted to it
Forbids it

phrases.english: Rav Yosef strongly objected to it:
Can space that is permitted to it
phrases.notes: The חצר, where carrying into the קרפף was already allowed

phrases.english: make it forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's reason: הואיל ואויר חצר מייתרו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Space that was already open for carrying into the קרפף should not be able to make the קרפף forbidden

steps.title: אביי: the space where the walls stood adds new area
steps.stepSummary: אביי replies that רב יוסף seems to follow רבי שמעון. Even according to רבי שמעון, though, the space where the fallen walls stood was never usable. That new space is what pushes the קרפף over the limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: According to whom? רבי שמעון? Even according to רבי שמעון, there is still the space where the walls stood.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב יוסף's challenge. He shows that new, never-permitted space does get added, so רבי זירא's ruling stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's idea that the חצר was already open to the קרפף only works according to רבי שמעון. רבי שמעון holds one may carry between a חצר and a קרפף. But even by רבי שמעון, the strip where the wall itself stood was solid wall, not open space. Once the wall falls, that strip is new open area added to the קרפף. If the קרפף was exactly בית סאתיים, this strip puts it over the limit.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom?
The place where the walls stood
But there is (still)

steps.whatToRemember: A קרפף fully breached into a חצר is forbidden. Even if the חצר's space doesn't count, the strip where the fallen wall stood is new space and can push the קרפף over בית סאתיים.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the חצר itself forbids the קרפף according to רבי שמעון. He is pointing only to the thin strip where the wall used to be.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
According to whom (are you speaking)? According to Rabbi Shimon?
phrases.notes: Only רבי שמעון allows carrying between a חצר and a קרפף

phrases.english: Even according to Rabbi Shimon,
there is still the space where the walls stood.
phrases.notes: That space was never open for carrying, so it is truly new area

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי כְּמַאן כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge from step 3 and defends רבי זירא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a different source of added space, the wall's former location, that was never permitted
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only added space is the חצר, which was already permitted, so it cannot forbid the קרפף
steps.terutzMaskana: Even by רבי שמעון, the strip where the walls stood is new open space, and it pushes the קרפף over בית סאתיים

steps.title: רב חסדא's ruling supports the fallen-wall-space idea
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that when a קרפף is fully breached into a חצר, the חצר stays permitted and the קרפף becomes forbidden. This backs up אביי's explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב חסדא said: a קרפף that was fully breached into a חצר: the חצר is permitted and the קרפף is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling from רב חסדא that fits אביי's point. The space of the fallen walls makes the קרפף forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the new space where the walls once stood pushes the קרפף over בית סאתיים. רב חסדא's ruling shows the same pattern: after the breach, only the קרפף becomes forbidden, while the חצר stays fine. This one-sided result needs an explanation, and the next steps provide it.

keyTerms.meaning: An enclosed open area, such as a yard or field, that was not fenced in for living purposes. One may carry there only if it is no larger than בית סאתיים.
Breached along its entire width, so the whole dividing wall is gone
Permitted / forbidden (here: for carrying on שבת)

phrases.english: As Rav Chisda said:
A karpef that was fully breached into a courtyard:
the courtyard is permitted and the karpef is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's answer in step 4 with a parallel ruling
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that the space of the fallen walls makes the קרפף exceed its limit
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב חסדא's ruling: חצר מותרת וקרפף אסור

steps.title: Why does the courtyard stay permitted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חצר is permitted. It suggests the reason might be the leftover pieces of wall on the חצר's side.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חצר: what is the reason it is permitted? Is it because it has remnants of wall at the sides of the opening?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the first half of רב חסדא's ruling. It offers a possible answer to test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the חצר is wider than the קרפף, pieces of the חצר's wall remain on both sides of the opening. Those pieces could make the gap look like a doorway, so the חצר would still count as enclosed. This is a suggested answer, not yet accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Wall remnants left on the sides of an opening, which make it look like an entrance

phrases.english: The courtyard: what is the reason it is permitted?
Because it has wall remnants on the sides?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רב חסדא's ruling
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the חצר remains permitted after the breach

steps.title: The wall-remnants reason doesn't always work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the wall-remnants reason. Sometimes the reverse happens: the קרפף keeps the remnants, yet the ruling stays the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: But sometimes you find it the opposite way!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggested reason. The case can be reversed, so wall remnants cannot be what makes the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חצר is narrower than the קרפף, it is the קרפף that keeps the wall remnants, while the חצר is open along its full width. רב חסדא's ruling makes no distinction between these cases, so the חצר is permitted either way. Therefore the reason must be something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Sometimes
The opposite, the reverse

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume 'fully breached' means the opening is the same size for both sides. The opening is the full width of the smaller area only. So whichever area is wider keeps wall remnants, and that could be either one.

phrases.english: But sometimes
you find it the opposite way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested answer in step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that גיפופי are the reason the חצר is permitted
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The remnants can be on the קרפף's side instead, yet the חצר is still permitted

steps.title: Extra wall-space only hurts the karpef
steps.stepSummary: The real reason: the space of the fallen walls pushes the קרפף over its size limit, but a חצר has no size limit, so the extra space does it no harm.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because we say: for this one (the קרפף), the space of the walls makes it too big; for that one (the חצר), the space of the walls does not make it too big.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct reason for רב חסדא's ruling. Size limits matter only for the קרפף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרפף not fenced in for living is limited to בית סאתיים, so the added space where the walls stood can push it over. A חצר was enclosed for living and has no size limit, so extra space changes nothing. This matches אביי's explanation in step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: The space where the walls used to stand
Makes it excessive, pushes it over the size limit
Rather (introduces the correct answer after a rejected one)

steps.whatToRemember: A breach between a חצר and a קרפף forbids only the קרפף. The reason is not wall remnants. The fallen walls' space adds to the קרפף's size and can push it past בית סאתיים, while a חצר has no size limit.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because we say:
this one: the space of the walls makes it too big,
and that one: the space of the walls does not make it too big.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reason with the correct one
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only the קרפף has a size limit, so only it is affected by the added space of the fallen walls
steps.whyThisMatters: This confirms the principle of אויר מחיצות that אביי used in step 4 to defend רבי זירא's ruling. רבי זירא's own stated reason was different: אויר חצר מייתרו, the courtyard's space.

steps.title: The orchard next to the mansion
steps.stepSummary: An orchard used the mansion's outer wall as one of its walls. When that wall fell, רב ביבי thought they could rely on the mansion's inner wall instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain orchard that was next to the wall of a mansion. The outer wall of the mansion fell. רב ביבי thought to say: let us rely on the inner wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new real-life case connected to fallen walls. It presents רב ביבי's first thought, which sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The orchard was bigger than בית סאתיים but was properly enclosed for living, and the mansion's outer wall served as one of its walls. Once that wall collapsed, רב ביבי wanted to treat the mansion's inner wall as the orchard's new wall. The language 'סבר... למימר' (he thought to say) signals that this view will likely be questioned.

keyTerms.meaning: An orchard
A mansion or palace
The outer wall
The inner wall
He thought to say (usually a first view that will be challenged)

phrases.english: A certain orchard
that was adjacent to the wall of a mansion.
The outer wall of the mansion fell.
Rav Beivai thought to say
let us rely on the inner wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא בּוּסְתָּנָא דַּהֲוָה סְמִיךְ לְגוּדָּא דְּאַפַּדְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new practical case about a fallen wall and whether another wall can replace it. It is related by topic (fallen walls), not built on the אויר מחיצות principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ביבי's initial view: the mansion's inner wall can serve as the orchard's wall after the outer wall fell

steps.title: רב פפי rejects relying on the mansion's inner wall
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי sharply rejects רב ביבי's suggestion. The mansion's inner walls were built to serve the inside of the house, not the orchard outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said to him: Because you come from short-lived people, you say cut-short ideas. These walls were made to serve the inside; they were not made to serve the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי rejects רב ביבי's idea from the previous step. He says the mansion's inner wall cannot replace the fallen outer wall for the orchard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wall counts for a space only if it was built to serve that space. The inner walls were built to close off the rooms of the mansion, not to enclose the orchard. So once the outer wall fell, the orchard lost a real wall and there is nothing valid to rely on.

keyTerms.meaning: Walls or partitions that define an enclosed area for the laws of carrying
For the inside (here, the inside of the mansion)
For the outside (here, the orchard outside the mansion)
Cut-short or short-lived people. This hints at רב ביבי's descent from the house of עלי, whose descendants were cursed with short lives
Cut-short or incomplete statements

steps.whatToRemember: A wall helps only the space it was built to serve. The inner walls of a house do not enclose the yard or orchard outside it.
steps.confusionAlert: The comment about 'short-lived people' is a sharp wordplay (מוּלָאֵי and מוּלְיָיאתָא). It is not the legal reason. The legal reason is the line about walls made for the inside and not for the outside.

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said to him:
Because you come from cut-short (short-lived) people
phrases.notes: He's hinting at the descendants of עלי הכהן, who were cursed with short lives.

phrases.english: you say cut-short (flawed) statements.
phrases.notes: It's a play on words: מוּלְיָיאתָא sounds like מוּלָאֵי, the cut-short people just mentioned.

phrases.english: These walls were made for the inside,
they were not made for the outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פַּפִּי: מִשּׁוּם דְּאַתּוּ מִמּוּלָאֵי אָמְרִיתוּ מִילֵּי מוּלְיָיאתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects רב ביבי's proposal from Step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects relying on the mansion's inner walls to enclose the orchard.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inner walls were built to serve the inside of the mansion, not the orchard outside, so they cannot count as the orchard's walls.

steps.title: The ריש גלותא asks for a way to eat in his orchard pavilion
steps.stepSummary: The ריש גלותא had a dining pavilion inside his large orchard. He asked רב הונא בר חיננא to arrange things so they could eat there on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a pavilion that the ריש גלותא had in his orchard. He said to רב הונא בר חיננא: Let the Master make an arrangement so that tomorrow we may eat bread there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about a real-life problem. This line sets up the case, and the next lines show how it was solved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The orchard was larger than two בית סאה and was not enclosed for living in, so it was forbidden to carry inside it. The ריש גלותא wanted to bring food and utensils from his house through the orchard to the pavilion. He needed a valid way to make that carrying permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: A pavilion or summer-house used for banquets
The Exilarch, the official leader of the Jews in Babylonia
An orchard or garden
An arrangement or fix that makes something permitted
Bread, here meaning a meal

phrases.english: There was a certain pavilion
that the Exilarch had in his orchard.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְרַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא:
phrases.english: He said to Rav Huna bar Chinnana:
Let the Master make an arrangement,
so that tomorrow (on Shabbat) we may eat bread there.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא אַבְּווֹרַנְקָא דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ לְרֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא בְּבוּסְתָּנֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new practical case about a large orchard that was not enclosed for living in.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: the ריש גלותא needs a way to carry through his large orchard to the pavilion on שבת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can carrying through the large orchard to the pavilion be permitted on שבת?

steps.title: רב הונא בר חיננא builds a reed fence, and רבא arrives
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חיננא put up reeds less than three handbreadths apart, making a valid walled corridor for living use. Then the גמרא says רבא went, which sets up his reaction.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and set up reed after reed, each less than three handbreadths apart. רבא went...
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר חיננא solves the problem by building fences of reeds to create a permitted path to the pavilion. The last words, 'רבא went', set up the next move, where רבא reacts to this fix.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the rule of לבוד, a gap smaller than three handbreadths counts as closed. So the reeds form real walls, newly built for the purpose of use, creating a walled corridor from the house to the pavilion. The words אֲזַל רָבָא prepare a challenge to this arrangement, which continues in the next part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: A reed
Less than three handbreadths
The rule that a gap under three handbreadths is treated as closed
He went

steps.confusionAlert: The reeds do not touch each other. They still count as a solid wall because each gap is less than three handbreadths, so the הלכה treats it as closed (לבוד).

phrases.english: He went and made (a fence of) reed after reed
less than three (handbreadths apart),
phrases.notes: Gaps under three handbreadths count as closed (לבוד).

phrases.english: Rava went
phrases.notes: Sets up רבא's reaction, which continues in the next section.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַל עֲבַד קָנֶה קָנֶה פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ריש גלותא's request from Step 11 and sets up רבא's coming response.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can carrying through the large orchard to the pavilion be permitted?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Build reed fences with gaps under three handbreadths, forming a valid walled corridor made for living use.
